Native activity / Read document source reconstruction

Image: installed Linux Steam 53.16 dwarfort
Identity: ELF:bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c
Method: original ELF unwind bodies, Itanium RTTI/vtables, immutable rel32
selectors, decoded literal stores, and Ghidra decompilation. Function names
in elf-decompiled.c are descriptive aliases rather than recovered symbols.

SOURCE FILES
elf-functions.tsv: original complete function extents and image identity.
elf-decompiled.c: Ghidra C for every function in that manifest.
elf-*.asm: complete instructions, with literal operands annotated.
elf-branches.tsv: both target and fallthrough of conditional branches.
elf-predicates.tsv: original compare, test and bit-test operands.
elf-switches.tsv: immutable selector-to-destination entries, including aliases.
elf-calls.tsv: direct and virtual supplier calls.
elf-literals.tsv: C strings, printable SIMD stores and immediate text stores.
elf-references.tsv: general_ref subclass, vtable and +0x98 text supplier.
written-productions.tsv: carrier, genre, style and quality source translations.
numbers/: decompiled libg_src_lib.so cardinal and ordinal suppliers.

ACTIVITY DOCUMENT OWNER: 0x15c1200..0x15c4863
The selected activity supplies a complete cyan heading through its +0xb8
caption method. The document then appends [C:7:0:0][B] and dispatches by
activity type. Its finite alternatives include considered/discussed/taught/
written scholarly topics, musical/poetic/dance performance and progress,
organizational activity messages, Read/Copy item descriptions, and the
no-specific-information default. Form/work lookups and empty names have
separate branches. See ../activity-detail/ for the full activity/form/caption
supplier graph and its display-productions.tsv; these clauses use the shared
activity-detail grammar rather than literal replacements in physical rows.

READ CAPTION: 0x1768590..0x17688a3
out = "Read"
if the activity has a first item reference:
    resolve that reference's item ID in the world item vector
    if found: out += " " + item_caption(item, flags=0, context=-1)
No reference, sentinel ID, empty vector, or missing item leaves exactly Read.
The item caption owns its complete book title, binding/material and quality
designation. Read is an activity verb. The title is not a personal name.
The bare Read job-title supplier is also retained at 0x1279380.

READ/COPY BODY
The activity document's Read/Copy cases resolve their referenced item and
append its complete item description through 0xe76ce0, not only its title.
That generator owns the initial This-is/These-are sentence, material and
item-specific branches, decoration/condition sentences and written carriers.
It uses page-carrier 0xe71100 and writing-carrier 0xe70c20 where appropriate.
The source remains one document before wrapping. The ordinary inventory
picture/Weight/state-action markers are not prerequisites for this window.

The independently retained read-details dispatcher 0x1782560 additionally
shows slab writing and page content, including the fixed alternatives
"It has no writing.", "The pages are blank." and "It has no pages.".
It is distinct from the activity-detail document owner above.

CARRIERS: 0xe70c20..0xe710fb and 0xe71100..0xe7168f
Writing lookup missing:
    "There used to be writing on the item.  "
Page work lookup missing:
    "The written portion consists of nothing."
Present page work:
    "The written portion consists of a " + decimal pages + " page "
Present writing:
    "Written on the item is " + article + " "
Title absent emits the untitled qualifier. Title present emits
" entitled " + the complete title. The 26 genre selectors, in order:
manual; guide; chronicle; short story; novel; biography; autobiography;
poem; play; letter; essay; dialog; musical composition; choreography;
comparative biography; biographical dictionary; genealogy; encyclopedia;
cultural history; cultural comparison; alternate history;
treatise on technological evolution; dictionary; star chart;
star catalogue; atlas.
Out-of-range genre emits no genre label but preserves the carrier, title,
author prefix, separator spaces and subsequent work body.
Author absent or lookup failure: no authored-by prefix.
Author lookup succeeds: append ", authored by " and its original/name
formatter's output. An unnamed author can leave "authored by .".
Append ".  " and work_body(work, mode). Mode controls native reference links,
not the semantic identity of the underlying names/events.

WORK BODY: 0xe6f720..0xe70c1a
References are counted by their parallel role vector, including empty text.
role 0: subjects. role 5: chapters.
No subjects: "The work has no particular subject.  "
One subject + alternate-history genre:
    'It asks the question, "What if ' + reference +
    ' had unfolded differently?"  '
One subject + genealogy genre:
    "It concerns the lineage of " + reference + ".  "
Otherwise: "It concerns " + role-0 references in source order;
    join intermediate subjects by ", ", final pair by " and "; end ".  ".
Empty references preserve their positions and separators, not the no-topic
branch. The runtime grammar includes their complete empty-field productions.

Second reference pass:
role 6: "The writing conveys a moral lesson regarding " + ref + ".  "
role 9: "The overall text emphasizes " + ref + ".  "
role 7: "For lyrics, the composer has selected " + ref + ".  "
role 8: "For musical accompaniment, the choreographer has selected " +
        ref + ".  "
Other roles: no sentence in this pass. Empty fields remain possible.

Styles:
No style records: omit the style sentence.
Otherwise: "The writing " + style(first, strength, quality).
If there is a second style: join by " and it " when their negative/positive
classification agrees, otherwise " yet it ", then append the second style.
Additional styles are not displayed. Always end the sentence with ".  ".
0xe66120 selects all 18 styles, strengths 0/1/2, and quality-dependent
alternatives. Default selector/strength emits no predicate; native connectors
still remain. Polarity supplier 0xe3e9b0 is retained separately.
Every emitted style phrase and empty-predicate sentence uses the existing
scoped writing vocabulary in legends-events.tsv.

Quality:
Genre 2/16/22/23/24/25: compilation of information.
Genre 7: poetry. Genre 12: composition. Genre 13: choreography.
Other genres, including default: prose.
Each category has six branches at quality thresholds 20/40/60/80/100.
All terminal phrases and the native "the splendid source" wording are
retained as source, with the caller's final ".  " accounted for.

Chapters:
Zero: no chapter sentences.
One: "The work has a single chapter.  " then "It covers " + ref + ".  ".
More than one: "The work has " + cardinal(count) + " chapters.  "; then
    "The " + lowercase ordinal(index + 1) + " chapter covers " + ref + ".  ".
The source uses libg_src_lib.so's get_number and get_ordinal, not a fixed
six-chapter list. Their complete compiled suppliers are in numbers/.

GENERAL REFERENCES
Every discovered general_ref vtable +0x98 supplier is retained, including
the inherited empty-description supplier. Nonempty families are written
works; poetic/musical/dance forms; language; values; scholarly knowledge;
interactions; artifacts; abstract buildings; historical events; historical
figures; spheres; sites; subregions; feature layers; entity populations;
creatures; item types; entities. Lookup failures, absent names and default
selectors can emit an empty field. Animated-corpse/ghost flags are independent.
Historical-event references dispatch to the event's +0xd8 title and retain
its actors, place and date. Their existing native history source catalogues
and runtime work-reference/work-sentence grammar remain authoritative.

RUNTIME OWNERS
src/activity_detail.inc: complete activity record and typed heading routing.
src/native_history_hooks.inc: retained activity rich box, paragraph boundaries
and original token identities/colors (resident/pet selectors use 0x26fb2f8).
src/dfcn.cpp: activity-document dispatch before generic screen matching.
src/fortress_item_descriptions.inc: visible Read-window item-document routing.
src/item_descriptions.inc: complete item/carrier/written-reference parsing.
data/runtime/legends-events.tsv: carrier, genre, style, quality/default text.
data/runtime/announcement-combat-grammar.tsv: typed subjects, lists, chapters.
data/runtime/announcement-description-grammar.tsv: other activity-detail text.
data/runtime/item-description-translations.tsv: item prose and binding nouns.

These files record original binary source and its semantic productions.
They are not observations of the running game or display results.
